text:
HSTU already supports objective-focused experiments: Meta’s [2024 reference configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin) uses sampled softmax, 128 negatives, normalized user/item embeddings and temperature 0.05. These establish practical starting points, not optimal settings for these Amazon categories. [Wu et al., 2024](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) explain sampled softmax’s implicit emphasis on hard negatives and show temperature sensitivity: excessively hard examples can dominate gradients. Objective and negative-count ablations therefore merit testing before adding representation features.

[Correcting the LogQ Correction, RecSys 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) revisits popularity-biased in-batch sampling: the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled. Its revised gradient applies importance sampling to negatives and introduces a detached uncertainty weight. The [authors’ implementation](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) includes uniform, in-batch and mixed-negative comparisons. Transfer the objective to the existing HSTU; changing backbone is unnecessary. Correction probabilities must describe the actual sampler; applying popularity logQ after deterministic hardest-item selection does not automatically yield a corrected estimator.

[AHNS, AAAI 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05191) adapts negative hardness to mitigate both uninformative negatives and potential false negatives; its evidence concerns collaborative filtering, so HSTU transfer remains a hypothesis. Practical experiment: score a bounded random candidate pool with the same HSTU, retain moderate-hardness samples, preserve random coverage, and exclude padding, targets and known training positives. Unknown positives remain unidentifiable from histories alone. Compare against uniform sampled softmax under fixed seeds and macro validation HR@10. The execution failure supplies no evidence that semantic enrichment or ranking deficiencies are the bottleneck.
